summary: On-chain multi-chain ERC-20 risk assessment. Validators agree on a 32-ordinal feature vector; every score is arithmetic over it.

adds: Deeper rug detection: HIDDEN_OWNER, UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, LOW_HOLDER_COUNT, CONCENTRATED_SUPPLY - four flags, all deterministic checks over explorer JSON, none of them asking the model anything.

Rescan and risk history: rescan_token(token_id), a previous score frozen onto every record, risk_delta, get_risk_history(token_id), get_history_by_address(token, chain, count), and a /history/[token] page.
Portfolio scanner: batch_scan(addresses, chain) over up to 5 tokens with on-chain aggregates, and a paste-addresses tab on /portfolio.
milestone.vector_change: 29 ordinals -> 32: hidden_owner, hold_lo, src_owner. _digest prefixes the hash with the canonical length, so a 1.1.0 hash (prefix 465) can never collide with a 1.0.0 one (prefix 422).
milestone.signature_change: get_risk_history now takes token_id. The address-addressed form is get_history_by_address(token_address, chain, count). RiskConsumer is unaffected - it only calls get_risk, is_safe, require_safe, check_rug_pull, get_badge and get_stats.
milestone.renames: UNVERIFIED -> UNVERIFIED_SOURCE and CONCENTRATED -> CONCENTRATED_SUPPLY, rather than adding duplicate flags that would double-count in batch_scan.total_rug_flags. CONCENTRATED_SUPPLY also moved from the 75% rung to the 50% one the name claims; the rug ladder still keys its severe rungs off 75%.

data_source: Blockscout /api/v2 for the five REST documents, plus one eth_call of owner() over JSON-RPC - publicnode first, Blockscout's own /api/eth-rpc as the fallback. All unauthenticated.

superseded.why_superseded: Four builds, and each one was fixed because something it did was visible on chain. Build 1 ran the owner probe after the model call rather than before it, and counted batch_scan's 5-address cap before de-duplicating. Build 2 fixed both, and then PEPE came back with src_owner 0 on its first round while the same URL answered 200 by hand seconds later - every 4xx was being read as 'this host has no such endpoint', so a throttle was being recorded as a property of the token. Build 3 classified 401/403/408/425/429 as transient, which is correct and also made rounds fail half the time: ten concurrent POSTs to Blockscout's /api/eth-rpc draw nine 429s, and a consensus round is a burst by construction. Build 4 leads with publicnode, which took the same burst with ten 200s and covers all four chains, and keeps Blockscout as the fallback. A second host is safe here because both read the same chain and the answer is one bit - it changes the odds of getting an answer, never the answer.

bradbury_blocker.measured_2026_09_19: Bradbury rejects eth_sendRawTransaction with 'gas limit too high' for any transaction whose gas limit exceeds 16,777,216 - exactly 2**24. Bisected: 16,777,216 deploys, 16,777,217 is refused. The block gas limit is 100,000,000, so this is a PER-TRANSACTION cap, not a block one.
bradbury_blocker.gas_model: Deploy gas is linear in source size at ~809.5 gas/byte plus ~240,000 fixed. Measured: 5,000 bytes -> 4,905,669 gas; 15,000 -> 12,573,064; 20,000 -> 16,640,019 (deploys); 21,000 -> 17,406,313 (refused); 50,779 (TokenScope 1.1.0 as measured) -> 40,479,983 (refused); the shipped 51,390-byte artifact projects to ~41.8M.
bradbury_blocker.not_a_milestone_regression: The 52,070-byte 1.0.0 artifact that is LIVE on Bradbury right now cannot be redeployed today either. That exact file was pulled from git and tried byte for byte, and was refused identically. A ten-line probe contract deploys fine, so the chain is healthy - the cap is the constraint.
bradbury_blocker.no_compression_route: GenVM's ZIP runner layout permits 'stored' only, no deflate (SDK spec, Runners -> Runner Layout -> ZIP Archive), so an archive is larger than the source rather than smaller.
bradbury_blocker.supersedes: The 2026-09-02 finding below, which measured a BLOCK PUBDATA ceiling between 53,000 and 53,700 bytes. That ceiling is still what the test suite budgets against, because it is the one that binds on Studionet and the one that will bind again on Bradbury if the gas cap is raised.
bradbury_blocker.cli_incompatibility: Separately: genlayer 0.40.0-rc.3 (2026-09-03) cannot talk to old-format Bradbury contracts at all - both reads and deploys fail, with 'runner comment does not start with version, using default v0.1.0' and 'call to private method Contract.__handle_undefined_method__'. 0.39.2 is the last release that speaks the format Bradbury's deployed contracts were built with, and every figure here was measured with it.
bradbury_blocker.reproduce: bash tools/deploy_bradbury.sh - it prints the projected gas against the cap before it tries, and says what it expects to happen. Full bisection in docs/PROBE.md section 11.

size_finding.claim: AuditCourt's notes put the GenVM runner deploy limit at 48 KB.
size_finding.measured_2026_08_31: That is stale. A 50,382-byte TokenScope artifact deployed successfully to BOTH Studionet and Bradbury.
size_finding.measured_2026_09_02: There IS a ceiling and it was found by walking into it. The 54,325-byte artifact carrying the watchlist was refused on Bradbury with 'invalid transaction: BlockPubdataLimitReached' at eth_estimateGas, followed by 'intrinsic gas too low' on the send. Padded probe contracts then bracketed it: 52,000 and 53,000 bytes both deployed, 53,700 was refused. So the ceiling sits between 53,000 and 53,700 bytes of source.
size_finding.how_it_was_fixed: Not by cutting the feature. tools/minify_contract.py gained a string-pooling pass that binds repeated literals to two-character module names — 'token_address' alone appears 15 times — which took the artifact from 54,325 to 52,070 bytes with no change to any string's value. Annotations, f-string fragments and match patterns are excluded, because in those three places a name and a literal do not mean the same thing.
size_finding.why_it_matters: It is a BLOCK pubdata limit, not a per-transaction one, so the exact figure depends on what else is in the block. The test suite budgets 53,000 rather than 53,700 for that reason.

cross_network_result.same_hash_across_networks: 422:41a76eee24bba743 with overall 86, produced independently on the new Studionet and Bradbury deployments by different validator sets.
cross_network_result.same_hash_across_artifacts: That is the SAME hash the pre-pooling 50,382-byte artifact produced on Bradbury on 2026-08-31. Binding repeated string literals to short names changed 2,255 bytes of source and not one of the 29 agreed ordinals - which is the check that matters, because the hash is a digest of the vector every validator independently reproduced.

cross_network_result.what_this_shows: Determinism is enforced WITHIN a round, with no tolerance. Across time a token's real distribution moves and a rung eventually gets crossed. Quantization absorbs the drift - a design comparing raw percentages would report a change where nothing material happened.

watchlist_result.why_moved_is_zero: A first score is not movement. baseline_seq 0 means the watcher never saw a score to move away from, so the entry reports NEW and is left out of the moved count - which is what makes `moved` mean 'something you were watching changed'.
